checklist.title: Passport Renewal Checklist
checklist.subtitle: Gather these before your embassy appointment.

items.applicationForm: Duly filled application form (use the Form Wizard below to prepare this)
items.cvForm: CV Form (collected at the embassy on the day)
items.taxReceipt: Original and a copy of your latest income tax payment receipt from the Myanmar Embassy
items.originalPassport: Original passport and a copy (photo page and validity page)
items.workPermit: Original and a copy of your Work Permit / S Pass / EP / PR card
items.photo: One recent passport photo (taken within 6 months, white background, ears visible, no glasses)
items.dependentDocs: If applying as a dependent: original and copy of Marriage Certificate / Birth Certificate / Household List

checklist.sourceDisclaimer: Based on the Myanmar Embassy Singapore's published application guidelines. Requirements can change — please confirm current requirements with the embassy before your appointment.
checklist.remittanceWarningTitle: Remittance rule that can affect your passport renewal
checklist.remittanceWarningBody: Since September 2023, Myanmar requires citizens working abroad to remit at least 25% of foreign wages home through an official bank or licensed remittance provider (not informal channels like hundi). Reports indicate non-compliance can affect passport renewal — keep proof of your official remittances. See Updates for details.

emergency.subtitle: Tap any number to call it. The red numbers are for danger right now; below them are the helplines for salary, health, abuse and scam problems.
emergency.missionSubtitle: For a lost passport, a death in the family, or when you need your own government's help.

safety.title: Abuse, violence and scams
safety.subtitle: When someone is hurting you or trying to take your money.

police.name: Police
police.hint: A crime, violence, or someone is in immediate danger.
police.smsHint: Not safe to speak? Text 70999 — say what is happening and exactly where you are.

ambulanceFire.name: Ambulance / Fire
ambulanceFire.hint: Life-threatening injury or illness, fire, or someone trapped.
ambulanceFire.smsHint: Deaf, hard of hearing or unable to speak? SCDF's emergency SMS is 70995.

momMdw.name: MOM Helpline for Domestic Workers
momMdw.hint: For domestic workers in distress — abuse, not enough food, unpaid salary, no rest day.
momMdw.hours: Mon–Fri, 8.30am–5.30pm. From overseas: +65 6339 5505. Your call is kept confidential.

mom.name: MOM Contact Centre
mom.hint: Ministry of Manpower — work pass questions and reports about salary, housing or illegal deployment.
mom.hours: Mon–Fri, 8.30am–5.30pm, except public holidays. Outside these hours, use the online form.

mwc.name: Migrant Workers' Centre (MWC)
mwc.hint: Salary disputes, workplace injury, repatriation and recruitment debt. Free legal advice at their Law Centre.
mwc.hours: 24 hours, in about 10 migrant worker languages.

cde.name: Centre for Domestic Employees (CDE)
cde.hint: Advice and mediation for domestic workers, and temporary shelter if you cannot stay in the house.

twc2.name: Transient Workers Count Too (TWC2)
twc2.hint: Help with salary claims and injury cases, plus free meals and help finding a place to stay.

home.name: HOME — Migrant Workers
home.hint: Employment advice and legal aid for non-domestic workers cheated or exploited by an employer or agent.
home.hours: Call, SMS or WhatsApp the same number. Help desk: 720 Geylang Road, Mon–Fri, 10am–5pm.

homeMdw.name: HOME — Domestic Workers
homeMdw.hint: Shelter, food and legal help if you are abused or exploited. Burmese-speaking help desk at Peninsula Plaza on Sundays.
homeMdw.hours: Call, SMS or WhatsApp the same number.

healthserve.name: HealthServe Crisis Helpline
healthserve.hint: Free counselling and medical help for migrant workers, with staff who speak your language.
healthserve.hours: 24 hours. Also runs a low-cost clinic and dental clinic in Geylang.

sos.name: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS)
sos.hint: If you feel hopeless or are thinking of ending your life, talk to someone now. Free and confidential.
sos.hours: 24 hours. If you cannot talk, message CareText on WhatsApp instead.

nurseFirst.name: NurseFirst
nurseFirst.hint: Sick but not an emergency, and unsure where to go? A nurse tells you which clinic to use.
nurseFirst.hours: For non-emergency medical advice. Cheaper than going to a hospital A&E.

nonEmergencyAmbulance.name: Non-Emergency Ambulance
nonEmergencyAmbulance.hint: Transport to hospital when the condition is not life-threatening. A fee applies.
nonEmergencyAmbulance.hours: SCDF will close this line on 1 January 2027. Never use it for a life-threatening case — call 995.

navh.name: National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline
navh.hint: Family violence, sexual harassment or abuse — including by an employer or a member of the household.
navh.hours: 24 hours. If the danger is happening now, call 999 first.

scamShield.name: ScamShield Helpline
scamShield.hint: Unsure whether a job offer, loan, agent fee or money request is a scam? Check before you pay anything.

policeHotline.name: Police Hotline (non-urgent)
policeHotline.hint: Give information or follow up on a case when nobody is in immediate danger.
policeHotline.hours: If you are in danger right now, call 999 instead.

prepare.location: Say where you are first — block and unit number, road name, or the nearest MRT station or landmark. Help can be sent while you explain the rest.
prepare.what: Then say what happened and whether anyone is hurt or bleeding.
prepare.identity: Have your name, work permit or FIN number, and your employer's or dormitory's name ready.
prepare.interpreter: Ask for an interpreter if English is difficult. 999, 995 and the worker helplines can find someone who speaks your language.
prepare.stay: Stay on the line until the operator tells you it is fine to hang up.
prepare.airtime: 1800 numbers are free from a landline, but your mobile plan may still charge airtime.
prepare.save: Save these numbers in your phone today. In an emergency you may have no data left to open this page.

emergency.verifiedNote: Numbers checked against each organisation's own website in September 2026. Opening hours and services change, so the official page linked on each card is always the final word.

accountsGuide.title: Essential Accounts Guide
accountsGuide.subtitle: Accounts that genuinely help you manage your money and access services safely in Singapore.
accountsGuide.bnplNote: This guide does not cover "Buy Now Pay Later" apps (e.g. Atome, Grab PayLater). They involve no credit check and real late fees that can snowball into debt — we recommend avoiding them, especially if you're already repaying recruitment fees.
accountsGuide.disclaimer: General information only — always confirm current steps on the official website, and ask your employer or the bank directly if unsure.

bank.name: Bank Account
bank.why: MOM requires your salary to be paid directly into your own bank account, not to your employer or an agent. A bank account also lets you save money and remit through official channels (required for Myanmar's 25% remittance rule).
bank.how: Bring your passport and Work Permit/S Pass card to a bank (e.g. POSB, DBS, OCBC, UOB). Some employers can help Work Permit holders open a POSB account via MOM's WP Online system — ask your employer first.

paynow.name: PayNow
paynow.why: PayNow lets you send and receive money instantly between banks for free using just a mobile number — used almost everywhere in Singapore, from splitting bills to paying small shops.
paynow.how: Open your bank's mobile app, find "PayNow" in the settings, and link it to your Singapore mobile number and bank account.

singpass.name: Singpass
singpass.why: Singpass is Singapore's official digital identity, used to access government e-services online (e.g. checking your Work Permit status, MOM services).
singpass.how: Work Permit holders can register at portal.singpass.gov.sg using your FIN, about 1-3 working days after your Work Permit is issued. You'll verify your identity with a live selfie (face verification).

grabpay.name: GrabPay Wallet (top-up only)
grabpay.why: A prepaid e-wallet for paying transport and food conveniently. Important: this is different from "GrabPay PayLater", which is a credit product — only use the top-up wallet, not PayLater.
grabpay.how: Download the Grab app, register with your mobile number, and top up the wallet using PayNow, bank transfer, or cash — never borrow through PayLater.

restDay.title: Rest Day Rights
restDay.subtitle: What Singapore law guarantees domestic and migrant workers about weekly rest days.

facts.oneRestDay: You are entitled to at least one rest day every week (about 4 per month), on a weekday agreed in advance with your employer — it does not have to be a Sunday.
facts.mandatoryOneDay: Since 1 January 2023, at least one rest day each month must be an actual day off — your employer cannot pay it away instead of giving you the day.
facts.compensation: For any other rest day you agree to work, your employer must either pay you at least one extra day's salary, or give you a full replacement day off within the same month.
facts.penalty: Employers who deny rest days can be fined up to S$5,000, and may lose their right to hire domestic workers — this is a serious offence, not a small matter.

restDay.reportTitle: If your rest days are being denied
restDay.reportSubtitle: Call MOM's dedicated helpline for domestic workers. This call is confidential.
restDay.sourceDisclaimer: Based on MOM's published rest-day regulations for migrant domestic workers (in force since January 2023). Rules can be updated — confirm current details with MOM if in doubt.

offDayGuide.title: Off-Day Guide
offDayGuide.subtitle: Real places in Singapore where migrant communities gather, shop and connect on rest days.

peninsulaPlaza.name: Peninsula Plaza ("Little Myanmar")
peninsulaPlaza.description: A shopping centre known as Singapore's Myanmar hub since the 1990s — Myanmar restaurants, grocery stores, travel agencies, and money changers, especially busy on Sundays.
peninsulaPlaza.food: Myanmar restaurants on the upper floors — mohinga, tea-leaf salad, curry and rice at prices close to home cooking.
peninsulaPlaza.gettingThere: City Hall MRT (NS25 / EW13), take Exit B and walk about 5 minutes. Busiest on Sunday afternoons.

burmeseTemple.name: Burmese Buddhist Temple
burmeseTemple.description: Singapore's only traditional Burmese-style Buddhist temple, founded in 1875 — a spiritual and cultural gathering point for the community.
burmeseTemple.food: No restaurant inside. Bring water; there are shops on Balestier Road, about 10 minutes' walk.
burmeseTemple.gettingThere: Toa Payoh MRT (NS19), then bus, or Novena MRT (NS20) and about 15 minutes' walk.

farrerPark.name: Farrer Park / Stamford Road area
farrerPark.description: An informal Sunday gathering spot near Little India where many Myanmar workers meet friends on their day off.
farrerPark.food: Every kind of South and Southeast Asian food in the surrounding streets, much of it under $6.
farrerPark.gettingThere: Farrer Park MRT (NE8). The crowd builds through Sunday afternoon and into the evening.

tekkaCentre.name: Tekka Centre, Little India
tekkaCentre.description: A wet market and hawker centre at the exit of Little India MRT, and the centre of Sunday life for South Asian workers — cheap food, money transfer shops, phone top-ups and the crowds along Serangoon Road. Open daily 6.30am–9pm.
tekkaCentre.food: Hawker centre downstairs — biryani, roti prata, fish head curry. Among the cheapest hot meals in the city.
tekkaCentre.gettingThere: Little India MRT (NE7 / DT12), the exit opens almost onto it. Open daily 6.30am–9pm.

bangladeshSquare.name: "Bangladesh Square", Desker Road
bangladeshSquare.description: The junction of Desker Road and Lembu Road, long known as the main Sunday meeting point for Bangladeshi workers. Busiest on Sunday evenings, with food stalls and Bengali groceries in the surrounding streets.
bangladeshSquare.food: Bengali restaurants and grocery shops through the surrounding streets, busiest on Sunday evening.
bangladeshSquare.gettingThere: Farrer Park MRT (NE8), then walk. Desker Road meets Lembu Road.

mustafa.name: Mustafa Centre
mustafa.description: A 24-hour department store near Farrer Park MRT, used for everything from groceries and phone cards to gold and remittance. Open at any hour, which matters if your rest day starts late.
mustafa.food: Food court inside, and the surrounding streets are full of cheap South Asian restaurants.
mustafa.gettingThere: Farrer Park MRT (NE8), about 3 minutes' walk. Open 24 hours.

peoplesPark.name: People's Park Complex, Chinatown
peoplesPark.description: A mall beside Chinatown MRT that is the main gathering point for workers from mainland China — regional Chinese food, money changers, remittance counters and travel agencies under one roof.
peoplesPark.food: Regional Chinese food court — Sichuan, Northeastern, Hunan — plus a hawker centre next door.
peoplesPark.gettingThere: Chinatown MRT (NE4 / DT19), the mall is right beside the station exit.

gardensByTheBay.name: Gardens by the Bay
gardensByTheBay.description: The Supertrees and the outdoor gardens are free to walk through, and the light show at the Supertree Grove runs free in the evening. The two glass domes (Flower Dome, Cloud Forest), the Skyway bridge and the Supertree Observatory all charge admission — you can have a full afternoon without paying for any of them.
gardensByTheBay.food: Hawker-priced food at Satay by the Bay, at the far end of the gardens. The cafes near the domes are tourist-priced.
gardensByTheBay.gettingThere: Bayfront MRT (CE1 / DT16), Exit B, then follow the underground link. About 10 minutes' walk to the Supertrees.

botanicGardens.name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
botanicGardens.description: A UNESCO World Heritage site, free to enter every day for everyone. Lawns, lakes, a rainforest trail and shade — the easiest place in Singapore to spend a whole day without spending money. Only the National Orchid Garden inside charges admission.
botanicGardens.food: Food court near the Tanglin Gate at ordinary prices; the restaurants inside are expensive. Bringing your own food is allowed and common.
botanicGardens.gettingThere: Botanic Gardens MRT (CC19 / DT9) opens directly onto the Bukit Timah Gate.

marinaBarrage.name: Marina Barrage
marinaBarrage.description: A dam with a grass roof, open 24 hours and free. The roof is one of the best places in Singapore to sit with a view of the whole skyline — people fly kites, picnic and stay till late. Popular with worker groups on Sundays.
marinaBarrage.food: Nothing much on site beyond a small shop. Most people bring food; there is a hawker centre at Marina South Pier or Satay by the Bay nearby.
marinaBarrage.gettingThere: No station at the door. Bayfront MRT (CE1 / DT16) then about 20 minutes' walk through Gardens by the Bay, or bus 400.

jewelChangi.name: Jewel Changi Airport
jewelChangi.description: The indoor waterfall — the Rain Vortex — is free to see, and free to sit and watch. In the evening it becomes a light and music show. You do not need a flight or a ticket to go in. The Canopy Park playgrounds and walkways upstairs are the part that charges.
jewelChangi.food: A very large food court in the basement at normal Singapore prices, plus every fast food chain.
jewelChangi.gettingThere: Changi Airport MRT (CG2), then follow signs — Jewel connects directly to Terminal 1. Rain Vortex runs 10am–10pm.

sentosa.name: Sentosa Island
sentosa.description:
A whole island that can cost you nothing, or a lot, depending entirely on how you go. Walking in across the Boardwalk from VivoCity is free — Sentosa's own site lists the admission charge for walking in as FREE. Once you are on the island, the Sentosa Express monorail, the island buses and the beach shuttle are all free to use, and the three beaches (Siloso, Palawan, Tanjong) cost nothing. So a full day of beach, sea and walking is genuinely free.

The paid part is the attractions. Universal Studios starts around $76, the Oceanarium around $43, Adventure Cove around $29, Wings of Time around $22. None of them is needed for a good day out.

Note: there is no Disneyland in Singapore — the theme park here is Universal Studios, on this island.
sentosa.food: Expensive at the resort side. Cheaper: eat at VivoCity's basement food court before you cross, or bring your own — the beaches allow picnics.
sentosa.gettingThere: HarbourFront MRT (NE1 / CC29), then VivoCity Lobby F on Level 1, and walk across the Boardwalk. Free, about 15 minutes. Part of the Boardwalk is closed for construction until around 2030 and walkers are redirected through a covered linkway — the route is still open, just signposted differently. The Sentosa Express from VivoCity costs $4 one way if you prefer to ride in.

offDayGuide.sourceDisclaimer: Locations are widely documented community gathering spots, not official recommendations. Please travel safely and let someone know your plans on your day off.
offDayGuide.noPlacesYet: We don't have {country} community places listed yet. Many Malaysians here live across the island rather than gathering in one area, so there is no single hub to point to — if you know one worth adding, tell us.
offDayGuide.museumWarningTitle: Museums are not free for work pass holders
offDayGuide.museumWarningBody: National Heritage Board museums — the National Museum, Asian Civilisations Museum and others — are free only for Singapore citizens and PRs. On a Work Permit, S Pass or Employment Pass you pay the full price (around $10 for an adult, $5 with a student or senior card). Worth knowing before you travel across the island expecting free entry.
offDayGuide.libraryNote: Public libraries are free to walk into, sit in air-conditioning and read all day — no membership needed for that. You only need a membership to borrow books home, and foreigners pay a yearly fee for it; check the current amount on NLB's site.

rates.title: SGD → {currency}
rates.disclaimer: Indicative rates collected from public sources — not a quote. Always confirm the exact rate with your provider before sending money.
rates.pageSubtitle: Indicative rates we have recorded, and where to check the real rate before you send money.
rates.checkIntro: Rates move during the day and every provider sets its own, so confirm the exact rate in the provider's own app before you send. What you can check here is more important: whether the company is licensed by MAS at all. If it is not on this list and your money goes missing, there is no regulator to complain to.
rates.providersNote: We are not affiliated with any provider and receive nothing if you use them.
rates.compareFee: Compare the total cost, not just the rate — a good rate with a high fee can be worse overall.
rates.compareLicence: Use a provider licensed by MAS. Unlicensed transfer means no recourse if the money disappears.
rates.panelDisclaimer: Indicative only. Rates for India, China, Bangladesh and Malaysia are the international mid-market rate — your provider's rate after fees will be lower. Myanmar's is from an independent rate-tracking site rather than a bank, since no bank or e-wallet here publishes a comparable daily figure — treat it as a rough indication only. Always confirm the exact rate in your provider's own app before you send.
rates.compareOfficial: Myanmar requires a share of overseas wages to be remitted through official channels. Keep your transfer receipts.

transport.title: Bus & MRT — how to travel in Singapore
transport.subtitle: How to pay, how fares are worked out, and the transfer rules that decide whether one trip counts as one journey or two.
transport.payIntro: You do not buy a ticket for each ride. You tap a card or phone at the reader.
transport.payCard: SimplyGo EZ-Link card — buy and top up at MRT station machines and convenience stores.
transport.payBank: A contactless bank card or phone wallet — tap it directly, no separate transit card needed.
transport.payBalance: Keep at least $5 on a SimplyGo EZ-Link card. Below that, the reader can reject it and you will not be able to board.
transport.payNoDisplay: SimplyGo cards do not show your fare or remaining balance at the gate. Check both in the SimplyGo app.
transport.payAxs: From 29 August 2026 you can no longer top up EZ-Link or SimplyGo cards at AXS machines. Use station machines, the app, or a convenience store.
transport.tapTitle: 2. Tap in and tap out — both times
transport.tapIn: Tap when you board the bus or enter the MRT gate.
transport.tapOut: Tap again when you get off the bus or leave the MRT gate.
transport.tapWarning: If you forget to tap out, you are charged the maximum fare for that line. This is the most common and most expensive mistake.
transport.fareDistance: Fares are based on the total distance of your whole journey, not the number of vehicles you take.
transport.fareTransfer: Changing between bus and train inside one journey does not start a new fare. You are charged once for the distance.
transport.transferIntro: Several trips count as one journey only if all of these are true:
transport.transferTime: No more than 2 hours between your first boarding and your last boarding in the journey.
transport.transferSameBus: You do not board the same bus service number twice in a row.
transport.transferStations: At Bukit Panjang, Newton and Tampines you must tap out of the first line and tap in again at the next. Do this within 15 minutes or it becomes a new journey with a new fare.
transport.mapsPlanner: LTA journey planner — official route and fare planner
transport.mapsFare: LTA fare calculator — check the cost before you travel
transport.mapsNetwork: LTA MRT and LRT system map
transport.mapsSimplyGo: SimplyGo — check your fares, balance and travel history
transport.mapsGoogle: Google Maps — live bus and train directions
transport.mapsTip: For a bus, the planner tells you the stop name and how many stops to stay on. Bus stops show the service numbers that stop there and a stop ID you can check in the app.
transport.mistake1: Forgetting to tap out — you pay the maximum fare.
transport.mistake2: Letting the balance fall below $5 — the reader rejects the card.
transport.mistake3: Taking a long break mid-journey — after 2 hours it becomes a new journey and you pay again.
transport.mistake4: Boarding the same bus number twice in a row — the second ride is charged as a new journey.
transport.disclaimer: Fares and rules are set by LTA and can change. Check the official links above before relying on anything here for a trip that matters.
